pages.text: $(thing)Vacuum Stability$(): a universe can fail before it starts. A vacuum energy larger by a factor of a hundred and no galaxy forms; the measured one is 10¹²⁰ times smaller than quantum theory's natural guess - the $(thing)cosmological constant problem$(). And the Higgs coupling runs downwards with energy until, near 10¹⁰ GeV, a deeper vacuum opens: ours is $(thing)metastable$(). The $(item)Higgs Field Modulator$() maps it into a $(item)Metastable Vacuum Lattice$().

$(thing)Creation from Nothing$(): quantise a whole closed universe and its wave function obeys the Wheeler-DeWitt equation. Vilenkin's universe tunnels through a barrier from no space at all; Hartle and Hawking's has no boundary - near the start time turns into space, and asking what came before is like asking what is south of the South Pole.
The $(item)Inflation Chamber$() folds spin foam, inflaton condensate and a metastable vacuum into a $(item)No-Boundary Seed$().
